content: The Save LIVES: A Road Safety Technical Package is a comprehensive guide developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2017 to address the global burden of road traffic injuries and fatalities. This package outlines evidence-based interventions aimed at reducing road traffic deaths and injuries, which claim approximately 1.25 million lives annually and cause non-fatal injuries to up to 50 million people worldwide. Nearly half of these fatalities involve vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians, cyclists, and motorcyclists. Road traffic crashes are the leading cause of death among individuals aged 15 to 29 years, representing a significant public health and socioeconomic challenge. The package emphasizes the importance of implementing a Safe System Approach, which recognizes human vulnerability and the inevitability of human error. This approach focuses on creating a forgiving road system that minimizes the risk of severe injuries or fatalities. The key components of the Safe System include safe roads and roadsides, safe speeds, safe vehicles, and safe road users. These elements work together to reduce crash forces and improve outcomes when crashes occur. The approach also highlights the shared responsibility of individuals, policymakers, road designers, and vehicle manufacturers in ensuring road safety. The Save LIVES package identifies six priority components for road safety interventions: 1. Speed Management: Establishing and enforcing speed limits, designing roads to calm traffic, and incorporating vehicle technologies to help drivers adhere to speed limits. Speeding significantly increases crash risk and severity, with even small increases in speed leading to higher rates of injury and fatal crashes. 2. Leadership on Road Safety: Strengthening institutional frameworks, policies, and governance to prioritize road safety at national and local levels. 3. Infrastructure Design and Improvement: Building and modifying roads to enhance safety for all users, including pedestrians and cyclists, while reducing crash risks. 4. Vehicle Safety Standards: Ensuring vehicles meet safety standards for crashworthiness and crash avoidance, incorporating technologies that protect occupants and other road users. 5. Enforcement of Traffic Laws: Implementing and enforcing laws related to speeding, seatbelt use, helmet use, and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. 6. Survival After a Crash: Improving emergency response systems, trauma care, and post-crash rehabilitation to reduce fatalities and long-term disabilities. It provides a framework for countries to assess their current road safety status, set measurable targets for improvement, and develop strategies to achieve these goals over the next five years and beyond. The Save LIVES package aligns with the United Nations' 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which includes ambitious targets to reduce road traffic deaths and injuries by 50% by 2020 and to provide access to safe, affordable, and sustainable transport systems by 2030. Despite progress in some high-income countries, road traffic deaths remain disproportionately high in lowand middle-income countries, which account for over 90% of global road traffic fatalities despite having only 54% of the world's registered vehicles. It draws on the experiences of countries like Sweden and the Netherlands, which have successfully reduced road traffic fatalities through integrated and evidence-based approaches. By adopting the interventions outlined in the Save LIVES package, countries can make significant strides in reducing the human and economic toll of road traffic crashes, ultimately fostering safer and more sustainable mobility for all.
